11.0.0.en: "Bethphage and Bethany": the two villages nearest to Jerusalem on the south-east side. The priests used to live in "Bethphage" because of its nearness to the temple, and the meaning of its name is "house of figs", because of the abundance of fig trees in it. And "Bethany" means "house of affliction", and in it lived Lazarus and his two sisters, and the Lord visited it often.

11.1.0.en: "A colt tied": as Christ drew near to Jerusalem, He sent two of His disciples (who represent the ministry of the two Covenants - the Old and the New) to the nearby village, to bring Him a colt to ride on His entry into Jerusalem. "Whereon never man sat": in this is a symbol of the virgin, pure heart that God needs from us, for God does not sit in a heart in which sin sits ... so let us hasten to repent, so that God may find a place for Himself in us ... And it is noticed that St. Matthew, in (Mt 21:7), says that the two disciples brought also the ass (the mother of this colt).

11.2.0.en: Since the Lord knew what the two disciples would meet when they went, He explained to them and guided them how to act with the owners of the colt; and what the Lord had told them happened exactly.

11.2.1.en: And this teaches us, beloved, that whoever holds fast to the Lord's commandments and the Church's guidance, the Lord subdues all opposers before him, and gives him grace before everyone with whom he deals...

11.2.2.en: So are you in fact careful not to move except by God's counsel and in obedience to Him in all your decisions, that you may experience and see how God prepares the way, and opens the closed doors before you?

11.3.0.en: The two disciples returned with the colt to the Lord, who consented to ride a colt as a symbol of humility and peace, and not a horse as a symbol of pomp and pride ... and so His love brought Him down from the Cherubic chariot to the colt!! As for the casting of garments on the colt, it was its preparation for His sitting on it ... and the symbolic meaning is the acceptance of Christ's headship and kingship, for the taking off of a garment in ancient times meant submission to those of honor ... and likewise many of the common people gathered around the Lord did, by spreading their garments, declaring their acceptance of Christ the King in the procession of His entry into Jerusalem, spreading and carrying olive branches, which symbolize peace, and palm branches, which symbolize victory.

11.4.0.en: "They that went before, and they that followed": some went before the Lord Christ in His procession, in a reference to the prophets and saints of the Old Testament who preceded His coming, and some followed Him, in a reference to the Apostles and the believers of the New Testament ... and the shout of all carried more than one meaning:

11.4.1.en: "Hosanna": it means "save us", and they meant that Christ was their awaited hope for their deliverance from the occupying Romans.

11.4.2.en: "Blessed is He that cometh": a passage from (v. 26) of (Ps 118), and it means that the One who comes is the one anointed by God and according to His will.

11.4.3.en: "Blessed be the kingdom ... of David": another declaration of hope that the hearts of the crowd were attached to Christ the King, who would restore to them the glories of the kingdom of Israel as in the days of David...

11.4.4.en: "Hosanna in the highest": that is, the awaited salvation has as its source the heavenly will of God.

11.4.5.en: My beloved brother ... Christ's entry into Jerusalem riding a colt is a lesson in which the Lord wanted to teach us humility ... was it not possible for Him to ride a horse? But He chose a simple procession, confirming what He had begun from His birth in a manger ... but as for you and me, what do we seek?! And why do we pursue the passing honor of the world?! My God ... teach me to follow Your example, and to learn from You how to be simple and humble in everything.

11.5.0.en: After a quick tour during which the Lord visited Jerusalem and the temple, He went out again to Bethany to spend the night, He and the Twelve, with Lazarus, Mary and Martha.

11.6.s.en: (2) The cursing of the fig tree

11.6.0.en: "On the morrow": on Monday morning, on His return to Jerusalem, He was hungry, that is, He was hungry for our good works which He expects from us. But what was our state, and the state of the Jewish nation in particular?! It had the outward appearance of faith (the abundance of leaves, as in v. 13), but without fruit, that is, without works.

11.7.0.en: "For the time of figs was not yet": was it hidden from Christ that it was not the time for the fig to bear fruit?!

11.7.1.en: Of course Christ knew before going to it that it had no figs ... and therefore we must understand these verses spiritually.

11.8.0.en: The Lord cursed the fig tree before His disciples, because: "every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire" (Mt 3:10).

11.8.1.en: This is a clear and strong warning from God to us all ... perhaps we are often like this tree, having the form and outward appearance of righteousness and godliness, and perhaps of service, without our having the real fruit that God hopes for from us ... would that you, my brother, sat in a quiet sitting and called yourself to account ... what if Christ came now and asked me for my fruits, what would I offer Him?!

11.8.2.en: "His disciples heard it": it shows the disciples' concentration on everything the Lord said. And this concentration and memorizing is the basis of Church tradition, that is, what the Apostles handed down orally to the following generations.

11.9.0.en: The aim of the visit to Jerusalem was the temple, of course, and when Christ entered it, He took care to cleanse it of the corruption that had attached to it, for merchants, thieves and bribe-takers had spread through it, with blemished sacrifices, and worship had turned into trade, and the house of God had become a market.

11.9.1.en: "Carry any vessel through the temple": because of the temple's central location in Jerusalem, some used it as a passage to shorten the way, entering by one gate and leaving by another, especially if they were carrying loads in order to save effort, so the Lord forbade them, because this conflicts with the honor of the house of God.

11.10.0.en: "And He taught": the Lord Jesus was not content with showing zeal and driving out the sellers, but gave teaching and explanation of what He was doing, and of the honor and reverence we must offer to the Church, the house of God, and He described His house as being for prayer and worship, and not a place for gain and profit-seeking, describing those who do that as thieves.

11.11.0.en: When the scribes and Pharisees saw the strength of Christ's authority in His work and in His teaching, and the people's being moved and their admiration for what He did, they feared Him, and feared for themselves - they being sinners - so feelings of envy, jealousy and anger seized them, and they sought to kill Him.

11.11.1.en: And in the evening, Christ returned to Bethany, where He would spend the night outside Jerusalem. My beloved brother ... the Church, the house of God and of the angels, David prayed and sang of it, saying: "Holiness becometh Thine house, O Lord, for ever (that is, to eternity)" (Ps 93:5). And how much we need to be an example to our children in teaching them how to respect the house of God ... for reverence, humility and silence during the prayers are among the most important matters to be observed, so that the heart may be occupied with God alone.

11.12.s.en: (4) The withered fig tree and the effectiveness of faith

11.12.0.en: And in the morning, that is, Tuesday, as they passed by, that is, were passing (on their way to Jerusalem), the disciples saw the cursed fig tree dried up from the roots, that is, down to its roots. And Peter was the first to notice that, and remembered yesterday, and addressed his words to Christ, calling Him to look at it!

11.13.0.en: "Have faith in God": that is, why do you marvel at what happened?! Where is your faith in God and in His power to do anything, He being the Creator by the Word? And Christ completed His talk with His disciples saying that faith, if it is without doubt, removes mountains, and that everything a man asks in faith according to God's will, he will obtain. But we must pray at all times with this faith, trusting in God's answer at the right time, and according to His goodness, and in what agrees with the way of the salvation of our souls.

11.13.1.en: My God and my good Savior ... I fear that I am a fig tree bearing nothing but leaves, but without fruit that pleases You. Therefore I ask You to be patient with me in Your longsuffering, and to make me care only for what You ask of me, and free me from my concern for people's opinion of me and my concern for myself and my appearance ... for all I want is for my life to be a sweet fruit in Your holy mouth...

11.14.0.en: After Christ had spoken about the answering of prayer, whose basis is faith, He set another condition for the answering of prayer, namely forgiveness for the one who has wronged us, and made clear that our forgiveness of the other is the basis of God's forgiveness of us. And perhaps we remember that after the Lord Christ taught us the Lord's Prayer, which contains many petitions, He commented on not one thing in all of it, except what He said here, namely that the condition of God's forgiveness of us is our forgiveness of the other (see Mt 6:14-15).

11.15.s.en: (5) The authority of the Lord Jesus

11.15.0.en: The cursed fig tree was on Christ's way to Jerusalem, and when He arrived with the disciples at the temple, the chief priests, the scribes and the Pharisees asked Him:

11.15.1.en: "By what authority doest Thou these things?": a question carrying two meanings of protest:

11.15.2.en: The first: what Christ did in cleansing the temple, and the fear and envy this stirred in their souls. The second: the authority of Christ's teaching the crowds in the temple; for whoever taught in the temple took a permit for this from the priests and elders...

11.15.3.en: And the overall meaning of this question is: who are you, that you teach, or drive out the sellers and money-changers and overturn their tables?!

11.16.0.en: Of course, and as was the Lord Christ's custom in His wisdom and His exposing of the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees, He answered their question only with a question that caused them confusion ... about the extent of their acknowledgment of John and his mission ... was it from God or a human claim of John's?!

11.17.0.en: St. Mark made clear the bewilderment into which the priests, scribes and elders fell as a result of Christ's question, and they reasoned that their answer would not be logical in any case, but would put them in a predicament before themselves because they had not believed John on the one hand, and before the people on the other hand, because they could not face the crowd by saying that John was an ordinary man.

11.18.0.en: And so the Lord did not give them the opportunity to bring any accusation against Him, or to try to seize Him, for they declared their inability before His wisdom...

11.18.1.en: Let us learn from the Lord, the source of all wisdom, how to answer the wicked who plot evil against us ... and we have no rescuer in these situations except quick prayer, lifting the heart before we speak, asking God's help.

11.18.2.en: The opposition to Christ in Jerusalem; His call to humility and giving

12.0.0.en: The Lord took advantage of the gathering of the people around Him in the temple, and spoke to them with this parable, intending to make clear what God suffered with the Jewish Church in the Old Testament.

12.0.1.en: "A certain man planted a vineyard": God, the founder, who called His people with great concern and exceeding care.

12.0.2.en: "Set an hedge ... digged a place for the winefat": that is, He guarded this vineyard with His strong hand, and the place for the winefat means that He prepared it to receive the good and the fruit of the vineyard's produce (that is, Christ the Savior, from the seed of this people, and suffering in the winepress).

12.0.3.en: "And built a tower": a tower or house for guarding, and it is the temple, and He delivered the people and the temple to the priests and the leaders, in whom He assumed the protection of His people, and gave them authority (went into a far country).

12.1.0.en: These verses show God's many attempts to visit His people through the successive prophets, and what the wicked people did to them, for there were those who despised His teaching, and those who beat him and wounded his head, that is, broke his head and nearly killed him, and others killed him in fact (like Isaiah) ... and so it was the lot of all generations of the prophets to be scourged and insulted, and the people and their priests forgot that by this they were insulting the owner of the vineyard Himself.

12.2.0.en: As an expression of the despair of the owner of the vineyard over attempts to reform the husbandmen, he sent his only son, who bears all the Father's authority, that perhaps they would reverence him and fear him and turn back from their evil.

12.3.0.en: Here the Lord Christ moves us in the parable to His present time, and to what would happen to Him, by the scheming of the wicked priests and scribes, in plotting against Him to kill Him and crucify Him outside the vineyard, that is, outside Jerusalem.

12.4.0.en: After the death of the Son, and the Jewish nation's continuing in refusing the last call from the Father - redemption - God rejects those who rejected Him and destroys the husbandmen, that is, the obstinate priests, and gives (transfers) the vineyard (the Church) to others (the Gentiles and the priesthood of the New Testament).

12.5.0.en: "Have ye not read": the accusation became clear and directed by Christ at the chief priests, scribes and elders, that what He said in the parable applies to them ... and He adds that what David said in (Ps 118:22-23), which they know well, applies to them and to Him, for they rejected Him, and He is the head of the corner.

12.5.1.en: "The head of the corner": that is, the cornerstone, which is the foundation stone at which the corners of the wall meet and which supports them, and it is like the concrete column of our time.

12.6.0.en: "And they sought to lay hold on Him": the listeners, elders and priests, understood that the parable was against them, and so rage overcame them, so that their decision was to kill Him. But the crowds gathered and loving the Lord's words were the only obstacle to their arresting Him, so they went away with their rage.

12.6.1.en: Give me, my God, a heart that realizes Your constant call to me, so that it responds to You and does not neglect Your commandments ... remove from it the hardness of the wicked husbandmen, that I may be obedient to You and to Your Church, doing all that I hear and learn.

12.7.0.en: The enemies gathered together to inform against the Lord Jesus and entrap Him. For the Pharisees are the learned, strict Jews, and they represent the Jewish nation. As for the Herodians, they are the followers of Herod, the representative of the occupying Romans in government. And they asked Him, after praising Him, so that He might lose His caution toward them, about the law of paying taxes to Caesar - the occupier - and in their craftiness, they bound their question with this phrase: "Shall we give, or shall we not give?" to confine His answer to yes or no. If He said yes, they would accuse Him of favoring Caesar and of loyalty to the Romans. And if He said no, they would accuse Him of hostility to Caesar and of inciting against him.

12.8.0.en: The Lord Christ exposed their deceit and purpose, and surprised them with the question: "Why tempt ye Me?"

12.8.1.en: And He completed His talk by asking for a penny - a Roman metal coin - and when it was brought, Christ asked a second question about whose were the image and the inscription on the two faces of the coin, and they answered: Caesar's.

12.9.0.en: Christ answered in His wisdom with an answer that none of them expected, but which disappointed their hopes of seizing Him or complaining against Him...

12.9.1.en: As for the spiritual meaning of the answer, it is: that we give the spirit its needs, and the body also, that is, that we not fall short in our attitudes and our faithfulness toward our duties in the world, but not at the expense of God and life with Him.

12.10.0.en: "The Sadducees": they are a Jewish sect who trace themselves to Zadok the high priest in the days of Solomon, and they came to Christ to tempt Him also, and they did not believe in the resurrection of the dead. St. Mark took care to point to their doctrine, so that we may understand the reason for their following question, which is not free of mockery of the resurrection, and reveals their limited material understanding of eternal life.

12.11.0.en: "Moses wrote": that is, in the legislation of the Law (Deut 25:5-6), that if a married man died before having children, his brother must marry the widow of the deceased, and register the first son in the name of the deceased, so that his name would not vanish from his tribe and his inheritance not be lost.

12.12.0.en: The Sadducees presented their controversial question with the aim of examining Christ, and of provoking the Pharisees, and of ridiculing the idea of the resurrection, namely: to which of the seven husbands will she be wife?! See the explanation of (Mt 22:

12.13.0.en: Christ's answer to them came rebuking, as He confronted them with the deviation of their faith, and attributed the reason for that to their turning away from God's law through rational disputation, and their making light of God's strength and power for the resurrection of the dead, and He made clear to them in (v. 25) that there is no bodily marriage in the resurrection, but the bodies will be spiritual and luminous like the bodies of the angels, so there is no need there for multiplying or procreation.

12.14.0.en: The Lord Christ returns to affirm the doctrine of the resurrection of the dead, and gives proof from the Holy Bible, for He reminds the Sadducees of the conversation that took place between God and Moses on Sinai, at the bush (Ex 3:6, 16), and how God presented Himself to Moses, when He said that He is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And it is not reasonable that God would ascribe Himself to the dead, but to the living. And Christ ended His talk as He had begun it with them, that they had deviated from the faith by their rejection of the truth of the resurrection from among the dead.

12.14.1.en: My beloved God ... the resurrection and eternity are a truth we believe in, but they are often absent from our hearts, so we are occupied with the perishing world, and forget what remains for us ... grant us, Lord, to care for "the things that remain instead of the things that perish, and the eternal instead of the temporal", as the Church teaches us to pray in the Litany of the Departed.

12.15.0.en: After the Pharisees had asked about tribute, and the Sadducees about the resurrection, it was the turn of the scribes, and one of them asked, having been pleased with the Lord Christ's answer to the Sadducees, by which He rebuked them and silenced them. The question of this scribe was: "Which is the first commandment of all?" that is, what is the commandment that can be considered the most important among the commandments?

12.16.0.en: The Lord Christ's answer came that God is one and He is the first before all things, and therefore the first commandment is that man love God with all his heart (his emotions), and with all his soul (his spirit), and with all his mind (his intellect), and with all his strength and effort (his ability). As for the second commandment, which is connected with it and completes it, it is man's love for any other man, for all human beings are relatives from one father, Adam, and Eve the one mother; and there is no commandment greater than these two, because they contain within them and outside them everything.

12.17.0.en: This scribe approved of Christ's answer, and testified to Him of his agreement with what He said, that God must be loved with the whole human being, and that love of the neighbor as oneself is the best sacrifice offered to God of all.

12.18.0.en: Christ rejoiced at the man's answer, and declared to him that he was not far from salvation.

12.18.1.en: And this declaration is for us all, for love of God and of man are the most important commandments of Christianity, and whoever strives in them gladdens God's heart.

12.18.2.en: And St. Mark mentions that Christ received no further questions from the sects of the Jews gathered around Him, and he also hinted that the reason was the comprehensive and decisive answer to everything He was asked about, so no one dared to ask Him again.

12.19.s.en: (5) Christ, son of David or Lord of David

12.19.0.en: "How say the scribes": the Lord Christ here began by taking the initiative with a question about what the scribes and Pharisees teach, that the awaited Christ is the son of David and of his seed. And this question had more than one reason: to make clear the ignorance of the Jewish teachers of the whole truth, and the shortcoming of their understanding, and then to prove His divinity by declaring that He Himself is the Lord of David.

12.20.0.en: The Lord Christ did not ask in order to receive an answer, but asked in order to answer and teach and make clear the following:

12.20.1.en: That David in (Ps 110:1) prophesies by the Holy Spirit and says: "The Lord said to my Lord", that is, the Father said to the Son: "Sit Thou on My right hand", that is, Yours is all My authority and My power, and I subdue all Your opposers and the kingdom of evil under Your feet, that is, under Your authority; how then can He be the son of David and his Lord at the same time ... and of course, what is meant is that Christ in His Incarnation came from the seed of David and the tribe of Judah, but He is the God worshiped by David, who calls Him: my Lord.

12.20.2.en: "The common people heard Him": St. Mark shows the difference between the joy of the simple people in Christ's teaching, and the rage of the priests and leaders at His talk.

12.21.s.en: (6) The warning against the scribes and Pharisees

12.21.0.en: The Lord Christ gives new teaching to the people which carries within it a rebuke of the scribes, for He warns them against behaving with pride and showiness like the scribes who wear the long robes, which is a long loose garment - like the Arab abaya - out of a desire to be distinguished, and who prefer places crowded with people such as the markets, to appear in them and exchange greetings ... likewise when they are invited to a gathering or a banquet, they take the best, most conspicuous places.

12.22.0.en: The Lord also exposes the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees, and reveals the sin of their material profit from the service, for they covet the money and inheritance of widows ... and even their prayers are not for God, but for people's praise of them.

12.22.1.en: Thus, it was necessary for the Lord Christ to reveal to us all the seriousness of the sin of pride, self-love and showiness, and how all this corrupts worship, and makes us, instead of enjoying God, only store up judgment for ourselves by our lack of humility and contrition ... so, my God, make me not care for my honor with those around me, but for You alone, for You are the One who searches and looks into my depths.

12.23.0.en: "Over against the treasury": that is, the box of the temple, where the people used to bring their offerings. And the expression "beheld how" means in the original Greek "continued to look", and it is a beautiful spiritual expression meaning that God is always looking at the offerings and gifts of His children, which express their love for Him. And the word "how" St. Mark mentioned as an introduction that God looks at the manner and the heart more than the amount and the appearance.

12.24.0.en: In the midst of the rich who give much, a poor woman came offering two mites, whose value was a farthing, that is, a quarter of the Roman coin at that time, equal to 1/40 of a denarius, and it was the least value and coin that existed ... and despite the smallness of the sum, Christ wanted to give the disciples new teaching, strange to human understanding and measure ... so the Lord considered that what the widow offered was, in God's eyes, more than all the large sums the rich paid, and made clear to them that the woman, though poor, gave God all she had and withheld nothing, while the others gave some of what they had.

12.24.1.en: And we learn two things here:

12.24.2.en: The first: that we do not judge anyone in what he offers, even if it is little, for God alone knows the circumstances of the person; perhaps someone who fasted one hour with weak health is better than another who fasted a whole day and in his fasting was careless in resisting his sins.

12.24.3.en: The second: that we not delay God's rights such as the tithes under the pretext of our financial need ... did not this woman offer all her living?!

12.24.4.en: Thirteen: signs of the destruction of Jerusalem and the end of the world; the necessity of spiritual vigilance. Introduction to the chapter:

12.24.5.en: This chapter corresponds exactly with (Mt 24), and its events took place on the Tuesday of Holy Week. And it contains prophecies relating to the destruction of Jerusalem in the year 70 A.D. at the hands of Titus the Roman commander (as will come in detail in v. 14), and others relating to the end of time and the second coming of Christ, and we must distinguish between them, and the interweaving of these signs goes back to two reasons:

12.24.6.en: (1) There was a strong belief among the Jews that the temple would not be ruined and demolished except at the end of the world and its passing away, and consequently the two events (the destruction of the temple and the end of the world) were linked as one event in the disciples' minds.

12.24.7.en: (2) Whether it is the destruction of Jerusalem and the death of thousands of Jews, or the end of the world, the lesson drawn from both is one, namely preparation by repentance, and therefore Christ's closing talk in this chapter was about preparation (vv. 32-37).
